probe_recovery.source_code: probe_test.py at git HEAD (deleted in the dirty worktree; inspected read-only with git show HEAD:probe_test.py)
probe_recovery.dataset_selection: 200 pairs selected by numpy default_rng(seed=42), sorted dataset indices
probe_recovery.preprocessing: tokenize with the local Ouro tokenizer, right truncation to 384 tokens, mean-pool mask-valid tokens separately for each candidate and loop
probe_recovery.feature_basis: post-final-norm layer-47 loop-boundary states, loops L1-L4 concatenated
probe_recovery.fit: full-batch torch.optim.LBFGS, strong_wolfe, mean logistic loss plus ||w||^2/(2*C*n), C=1
probe_recovery.split: symmetric +/- rows followed by numpy RandomState(42) permutation and 80/20 row split: 320 train rows, 80 eval rows
probe_recovery.split_caveat: The historical protocol splits +/- orientations at row level; opposite orientations of a source HH pair can cross train/eval. The 80 eval rows represent 74 unique source pairs. The reported CI clusters by source pair.
probe_recovery.reconstruction_sanity: Thinking accuracy 0.8375 is within 0.75 percentage points of the documented approximately 0.845 result.

recommended_paper_patches.section_3_7: In a targeted replication using the bias-free antisymmetric linear difference probe, the same held-out HH accuracy was obtained for base Ouro-2.6B, Ouro-2.6B-Thinking, and Ouro-RLTT (83.75% for each; exact swap consistency 1.0). Thus the earlier 24%/95.2%/95.0% separation is specific to the fixed-order high-capacity evaluator and does not establish training-stage localization in the clean relational units. We therefore do not claim that reasoning/RL training installs the linearly readable relational preference signal; resolving training-stage localization requires a larger independently pair-split antisymmetric replication.
recommended_paper_patches.section_5: At the strict pre-answer cut, adding hidden features to the length-and-log-probability baseline raises AUROC from 0.731 to 0.797 (incremental ΔAUROC +0.066). A paired task-clustered bootstrap over 170 GSM8K problems (10,000 draws; all four candidates retained per sampled problem) gives a 95% CI of [+0.021, +0.112], which excludes zero. The improvement is therefore statistically significant under task-clustered resampling, while remaining a modest incremental effect demonstrated in one powered domain.

remaining_blockers: The original approximately 84.5% probe weights were not saved; Check 1 necessarily uses a reconstruction.
The historical +/- row split permits opposite orientations of the same HH pair to cross train/eval; a larger independent pair-level split is needed for a definitive localization study.
The exact code/draws that produced the historical pre-answer CI [0.0172, 0.1144] were not preserved, although the new task-clustered recomputation independently verifies exclusion of zero.
The local RLTT checkpoint has no embedded upstream revision; shard hashes are recorded instead.
